# runr_project (Resource)

A RunR project: a function (`faas`), a single-file script (`xaas`) or a container (`caas`) in a region. Code is uploaded with `runr deploy`; container images and deployments can be managed with `runr_deployment`.

A config change saves a new project version; running deployments pick it up when they are redeployed (see `runr_deployment.triggers`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "runr_region" "eu" {
  name = "eu-1"
}

# A Python function; its code is uploaded with `runr deploy`.
resource "runr_project" "api" {
  name      = "orders-api"
  type      = "faas"
  runtime   = "python"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id
  handler   = "main.handler"

  resources = {
    cpu             = "250m"
    memory_mb       = 256
    timeout_seconds = 30
  }

  scale = {
    min     = 0
    max     = 10
    to_zero = true
  }

  # Timed warmer: 3 containers warm on weekdays from 09:00, none from 18:00 (organization time zone)
  scale_schedule = [
    { cron = "0 9 * * 1-5", min_scale = 3 },
    { cron = "0 18 * * 1-5", min_scale = 0 },
  ]

  trigger = {
    type = "http"
  }
}

# A nightly job at 02:00 Berlin time ("" or left out on a new schedule: the organization's zone).
resource "runr_project" "report" {
  name      = "nightly-report"
  type      = "faas"
  runtime   = "nodejs"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id

  trigger = {
    type     = "schedule"
    schedule = "0 2 * * *"
    timezone = "Europe/Berlin"
  }
}

# A container.
resource "runr_project" "web" {
  name      = "web"
  type      = "caas"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id
  image     = "ghcr.io/acme/web:1.4.2"
  ports     = [8080]

  # Let runr_deployment (or CI) roll out new images.
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [image]
  }
}

# The whole trigger list: HTTP requests, a schedule, a Kafka topic and a webhook inbox.
resource "runr_project" "orders" {
  name      = "orders"
  type      = "faas"
  runtime   = "python"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id

  triggers = [
    { type = "http" },
    {
      name   = "nightly"
      type   = "schedule"
      config = jsonencode({ cron = "0 2 * * *", timezone = "Europe/Berlin" })
    },
    {
      name    = "orders"
      type    = "kafka"
      config  = jsonencode({ brokers = ["kafka-1:9092"], topic = "orders", sasl = { mechanism = "scram-sha-512", username = "orders" } })
      secrets = { sasl_password = var.kafka_password }
    },
    {
      name    = "github"
      type    = "webhook"
      config  = jsonencode({ verify = "github" })
      secrets = { signing_secret = var.github_webhook_secret }
    },
  ]

  # No public URL: only the orders-api project calls it, on the region's internal network.
  network = {
    access_mode = "internal"
    callers     = [runr_project.api.network.internal_name]
  }

  # New versions take 10 %, then 50 % of the traffic, five minutes each.
  deploy_strategy = {
    strategy = "canary"
    canary = {
      steps                = [10, 50]
      interval_minutes     = 5
      error_rate_threshold = 2
    }
  }
}

# A global project: the primary region (region_id) and a standby region behind one host name.
data "runr_region" "us" {
  name = "us-1"
}

resource "runr_project" "shop" {
  name      = "shop"
  type      = "caas"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id
  image     = "ghcr.io/acme/shop:2.0.0"
  ports     = [8080]

  global = {
    regions  = [data.runr_region.eu.id, data.runr_region.us.id]
    mode     = "ha"
    failover = "automatic"
  }
}

variable "kafka_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "github_webhook_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Project name; its slug names the service and the default URL. Changing it creates a new project.
- `region_id` (String) Region id (`data.runr_region`). Changing it moves the project.
- `type` (String) `faas`, `xaas` or `caas`. Changing it creates a new project.

### Optional

- `args` (List of String) `caas`: arguments.
- `command` (List of String) `caas`: entrypoint override.
- `deploy_strategy` (Attributes) How a deploy rolls out ([deploy strategies](https://runr.sh/docs/deploy-strategies/)): `direct`, `blue_green` or `canary` with the options of both. Values left out stay as they are; the project's environments use these settings unless they set their own. Promotion, abort and rollback of a rollout stay with `runr rollout`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--deploy_strategy))
- `description` (String) Free text.
- `filename` (String) `xaas`: the script file (default `main.<ext>`).
- `global` (Attributes) A global project ([global projects](https://runr.sh/docs/global-projects/)): the project runs in every region of `regions` behind one host name, `region_id` is its primary region. A project is created global or regional: adding `global` to a regional project replaces it. Left out, a global project stays as it is. The regions need global DNS. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--global))
- `handler` (String) `faas`: `file.function` (default `main.handler` → `main.py`, `def handler`). `xaas`: the function name (default `handler`).
- `image` (String) `caas`: container image. Required when the project is created.
- `network` (Attributes) Who reaches the project ([internal network](https://runr.sh/docs/internal-network/)). Values left out stay as they are. Changing the access mode or the allow list needs `network.manage`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network))
- `ports` (List of Number) `caas`: container ports; the first serves HTTP (default 80).
- `resources` (Attributes) Container limits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resources))
- `runtime` (String) Runtime of `faas`/`xaas` projects: `python`, `nodejs`, `go`, `php`, … Changing it creates a new project.
- `runtime_version` (String) Runtime version; default the platform's default version. Changing it creates a new project.
- `scale` (Attributes) Autoscaling range. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scale))
- `scale_schedule` (Attributes List) Timed warmer: each row keeps at least `min_scale` containers warm from the moment its five-field `cron` expression fires until the next row fires. The expressions run in the organization's time zone (its Time zone setting, default Europe/Istanbul). While rows are set they replace `scale.min`; `scale.max` still applies. RunR applies a changed schedule to the running workload within a minute, without a redeploy. At most 10 rows; `[]` turns the warmer off, leaving the attribute out keeps the project's schedule as it is. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scale_schedule))
- `trigger` (Attributes) What starts the code: the project's primary trigger, the first enabled one of its trigger list. Setting it changes the primary trigger's type and settings and leaves the project's other triggers as they are; `triggers` sets the whole list instead (set either `trigger` or `triggers`). Read back, it is the primary trigger, which can be of a type only `triggers` sets (e.g. `webhook` or `kafka`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trigger))
- `triggers` (Attributes List) The project's whole trigger list, in order: the first enabled trigger is the primary one (`trigger` reads it back). Set, the list replaces the project's list — a trigger whose `name` and `type` match one the project has keeps its secrets, webhook inbox URL and stored events; the others are created or removed. Left out, the list stays as it is (and `trigger` can set the primary trigger). Set either `trigger` or `triggers`. A change reaches the running deployment with the next deploy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--triggers))

### Read-Only

- `endpoint_url` (String) Public URL (HTTP trigger).
- `id` (String) Project id.
- `latest_version_id` (String) Id of the newest version.
- `slug` (String) Slug derived from the name.

<a id="nestedatt--deploy_strategy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `deploy_strategy`

Optional:

- `blue_green` (Attributes) Options of the blue-green strategy. Left out, the options stay as they are. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--deploy_strategy--blue_green))
- `canary` (Attributes) Options of the canary strategy. Left out, the options stay as they are. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--deploy_strategy--canary))
- `strategy` (String) `direct` (the new revision replaces the live one once it is ready), `blue_green` or `canary`. A strategy other than `direct` needs an `http` or `workflow` trigger.

<a id="nestedatt--deploy_strategy--blue_green"></a>
### Nested Schema for `deploy_strategy.blue_green`

Optional:

- `auto_promote` (Boolean) Promote once the health checks passed; `false` waits for `runr rollout promote`.
- `health_checks` (Number) Consecutive 2xx answers auto promotion needs (1-20, one every 10 s).
- `health_path` (String) Path the health checks call, e.g. `/healthz`. Not set in a configured `blue_green` block: the new revision's readiness alone decides.
- `keep_previous_minutes` (Number) Minutes the previous revision stays warm after promotion for an instant rollback (0-1440).


<a id="nestedatt--deploy_strategy--canary"></a>
### Nested Schema for `deploy_strategy.canary`

Optional:

- `error_rate_threshold` (Number) Roll back above this error rate of the new revision in percent (0-100). Not set in a configured `canary` block: not checked.
- `interval_minutes` (Number) How long each step lasts (1-1440 minutes).
- `p95_threshold_ms` (Number) Roll back above this 95th percentile latency in milliseconds (1-600000). Not set in a configured `canary` block: not checked.
- `steps` (List of Number) Traffic percentages of the new revision, strictly increasing (1-10 steps, 1-100); reaching 100 promotes it.



<a id="nestedatt--global"></a>
### Nested Schema for `global`

Required:

- `regions` (List of String) Region ids in HA order (2-8), `region_id` (the primary) among them. A region left out has its copy removed; a new one gets the active version.

Optional:

- `failover` (String) `automatic` (default: RunR moves the primary when its health check keeps failing) or `manual` (`runr projects global failover`).
- `mode` (String) `ha` (default: DNS answers the primary while it is healthy, the others when it is not) or `proximity` (the healthy region closest to the client).

Read-Only:

- `bindings` (Attributes List) How the project's bindings are reached from every region: `access` is `direct` (an external binding), `link` (the data link to its home region) or `replicas` (a replica cluster in every region). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--global--bindings))
- `failover_after_seconds` (Number) How long the primary's health check fails before an automatic failover.
- `hostname` (String) The global host name `<slug>.<zone>` (empty while the platform has no base domain).

<a id="nestedatt--global--bindings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `global.bindings`

Read-Only:

- `access` (String) `direct`, `link` or `replicas`.
- `binding_id` (String) Binding id.
- `home_region_id` (String) The region its data lives in.
- `name` (String) Binding name.
- `type` (String) Binding type.



<a id="nestedatt--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network`

Optional:

- `access_mode` (String) `public` (anyone reaches the public URL; the default), `allowlist` (the public URL answers `allowed_cidrs` only) or `internal` (no public URL: the projects in `callers` call it on the region's internal network).
- `allowed_cidrs` (Set of String) IP addresses or CIDR ranges the public URL answers in `allowlist` mode (empty in the other modes).
- `callers` (Set of String) Projects allowed to call this one on the internal network, by internal name `<project>.<organization>` (another project's `network.internal_name`; another organization's project where the platform allows it). Set, it is the whole allow list; `[]` removes every caller.

Read-Only:

- `internal_name` (String) The project's internal name `<project>.<organization>`, for other projects' `callers`.
- `internal_url` (String) The URL other projects of the region call it at on the internal network.


<a id="nestedatt--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources`

Optional:

- `cpu` (String) Kubernetes CPU quantity (`100m`, `0.5`).
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory in MB (at least 64).
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Request timeout in seconds.


<a id="nestedatt--scale"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scale`

Optional:

- `max` (Number) Maximum instances (1-1000).
- `min` (Number) Minimum instances (0-10).
- `to_zero` (Boolean) Scale to zero instances when idle.


<a id="nestedatt--scale_schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scale_schedule`

Required:

- `cron` (String) Five-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), fields separated by one space, e.g. `0 9 * * 1-5`.
- `min_scale` (Number) Containers kept warm from this moment on (0-10, at most `scale.max`).


<a id="nestedatt--trigger"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger`

Optional:

- `queue` (String) Redis stream of a `queue` trigger (the region needs Redis).
- `schedule` (String) Cron expression of a `schedule` trigger, e.g. `*/5 * * * *`.
- `timezone` (String) IANA time zone the `schedule` runs in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin` or `UTC`. `""` runs it in the organization's time zone (its Time zone setting, default Europe/Istanbul), which it then follows. Leaving it out keeps the schedule's zone: a new schedule runs in the organization's, one created before RunR 0.6.0 in UTC.
- `type` (String) `http` (default), `schedule`, `queue` or `workflow` (a durable workflow project; its only trigger). Reads back the primary trigger's type, which can be one `triggers` sets (e.g. `webhook` or `kafka`).

Read-Only:

- `effective_timezone` (String) The time zone the `schedule` runs in: `timezone`, else the organization's; null without a schedule.


<a id="nestedatt--triggers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `triggers`

Required:

- `type` (String) `http`, `schedule`, `queue`, `workflow`, `webhook`, `topic`, `platform_event` or an event source: `kafka`, `nats`, `rabbitmq`, `mqtt`, `cdc` (Postgres logical replication), `email` (IMAP) or `s3`. At most one `http` trigger; a `workflow` trigger is the project's only one.

Optional:

- `config` (String) The type's settings as JSON (`jsonencode({...})`), e.g. `{cron = "0 2 * * *", timezone = "Europe/Berlin"}` for a schedule, `{brokers = ["kafka:9092"], topic = "orders"}` for kafka, or `{verify = "github"}` for a webhook; [triggers](https://runr.sh/docs/triggers/) lists every type's settings. RunR fills in defaults: the state keeps this JSON while RunR's config holds every value it sets, and shows RunR's config when a value differs. Left out: RunR's config of the trigger (`{}` for `http`).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the trigger runs (default `true`).
- `name` (String) Name, unique in the project (lower-case letters, digits and dashes). Default: the type (`schedule`, then `schedule-2`, …). Name triggers whose secrets or inbox URL must survive a reordering.
- `secrets` (Map of String, Sensitive) Write-only secrets of the type: `signing_secret` (webhook), `sasl_password` (kafka), `password` / `token` / `nkey_seed` / `creds` (nats), `url` (rabbitmq), `password` (mqtt, email), `dsn` (cdc), `access_key` and `secret_key` (s3). RunR lists only their names; Terraform keeps the values it set and sets a secret again when it was removed outside Terraform. Set, the map is the trigger's whole set (a secret it leaves out is removed); left out, the trigger's secrets stay as they are.

Read-Only:

- `effective_timezone` (String) The time zone a `schedule` runs in: its `timezone`, else the organization's.
- `id` (String) Trigger id.
- `primary` (Boolean) Whether it is the primary trigger (the first enabled one).
- `runs_on` (String) What runs it: `service` (the project's service), `gateway` (its event gateway), `cronjob` or `disabled`.
- `secret_names` (List of String) The names of the secrets the trigger has.
- `url` (String) The public inbox URL of a `webhook` trigger (send the provider's webhooks there).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A project is imported by name or id.
terraform import runr_project.api orders-api
```
